clue.text: Blundering doctor-left one inside incensed

indicators.note: the doctor, left and one pieces are placed inside the word for incensed

parts.note: incensed, as by an insult, means stung
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A furious doctor who has just walked out is making a mess of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tripping over their words or feet is floundering clumsily, which is what blundering describes.

clue.text: Gets a bite

parts.note: read literally, acquiring the means to bite: what a baby does when its first teeth come through, not an angler's nibble

explanation.surface: An angler finally gets something on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fishing or an insect; the cryptic reading is of an infant cutting its first teeth, gaining something to bite with.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby cutting its first teeth is acquiring its means of biting, a playful cryptic sense.

clue.text: Cunning in short at obtaining cocktail

indicators.note: the word for cunning is placed in the word for short

parts.note: mini means short, as in a short skirt
art can mean cunning or craft, as in artful

explanation.surface: Someone with a knack is trying to get hold of a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at obtaining' serves only as link words joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth drink served in a stemmed glass is the classic example of a cocktail.

clue.text: Support a point put concerning an ambassador

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a tine is a point or prong of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A diplomat's case is being propped up with a sharp argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link word. A legate is a papal envoy, so the adjective describes matters relating to such an envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a papal envoy, so the adjective describes what relates to such a representative.

clue.text: There's a number in blood-quite a lot

indicators.note: the letters for a number are put in the word for blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

explanation.surface: A blood test reveals a high count of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed after a noun, the word means in abundance, plenty.

clue.text: The concierge cannot be lackadaisical

parts.note: someone who looks after a building must by name take care, so cannot be careless

explanation.surface: A hotel doorman must never be slack on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue plays on the job title split as one who takes care, therefore never careless.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to look after a building is a janitor or porter, much like a concierge.

clue.text: Finery and excellent drink brought back

indicators.note: brought back signals that the words for excellent and drink are read in reverse order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the letter I for the figure one
lager is a drink, a pale beer

explanation.surface: Fine clothes and top-quality liquor are being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns AILAGER round, giving the answer. A1 means first-class, with I standing in for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial robes and emblems of royalty are showy clothes, so the word means finery.

clue.text: Rose cut in rudely, being stupid

indicators.note: rudely signals that the letters of rose cut in are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Rose barged into the conversation rudely, which was a silly thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name or a flower; it is just anagram material, with 'being' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic and dim-witted behaviour is described this way, a harsh synonym for stupid.

clue.text: Non-professional with a mature appearance

indicators.note: appearance suggests a new look for the letters of a mature, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unpaid enthusiast who looks older than their years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'appearance' signals that A MATURE takes a new form.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist who does something without being paid is a non-professional, the opposite of a pro.

clue.text: The aristocracy want an attendant around always

indicators.note: the word for attendant goes around the word for always

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Lords and ladies demand a servant at their side at all times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' is a link word. EER is the poetic e'er, meaning always.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers of the realm as a body make up the nobility, the aristocracy.

clue.text: When done, carry out ham

parts.note: over means done or finished
to act is to carry out or perform

explanation.surface: Once a job is finished, take out the ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like a meat; it is the verb for performing in an exaggerated way. 'When' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to play a role with exaggerated, theatrical emphasis.

clue.text: Saving more, but still row about end-of-month gap

indicators.note: the word for row goes about the end letter of month and the word for gap

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: end of month picks out the final letter of that word

parts.note: a rift is a gap or split

explanation.surface: Someone is putting more aside, though still quarrelling over a cash shortfall at the month's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but still' is a link. 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of frugal, describing one who economises to a greater degree.

clue.text: Finish with awfully sore back

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of sore are badly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is ending up with a terribly painful back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the body; it is the verb meaning support. 'awfully' scrambles SORE into ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate is to give them your approval and support.

clue.text: Somehow get in a no-a denial

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of get in a no are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Somehow manage to slip in a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not so is a contradiction or refusal, which is a denial.

clue.text: Give a small mark

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a sign is a mark or symbol

explanation.surface: A teacher awards a low grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or hand over a task to someone is to give it to them.

clue.text: With a reversible cushion furniture is versatile

indicators.note: reversible means the word for cushion is read backwards

parts.note: a pad is a cushion
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: Furniture with a reversible cushion can be used in many ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversible' looks like a description of the cushion; it turns PAD into DAP. 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to adjust to new situations or uses, so flexible and versatile.

clue.text: Restaurant where the newly-wed will receive a flower

indicators.note: the word for newly-wed will receive another word inside it

parts.note: a groom is a newly married man
a rill is a small stream, something that flows

explanation.surface: A dining venue where a bridegroom is presented with a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as a bloom, but it is a crossword pun on something that flows, a stream. 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant specialising in grilled food served to order, so a type of eatery.

clue.text: Angst resulting from dealing with code

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with, as in a letter heading
Morse is the telegraphic code of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Anxiety arising from struggling with a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resulting from' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep regret and guilt over a wrong is a kind of anguish, close to angst.

clue.text: Split due to stuff about English standard

indicators.note: the word for stuff goes about the letters for English and standard

parts.note: to sate is to stuff or fill up with food
par is a standard or norm, as in up to par

explanation.surface: A couple broke up over a dispute about proper English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is a link phrase. 'stuff' looks like a noun but is the verb, to fill full.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide or part company is to split.

clue.text: Key in a single item, feeling irritated

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

indicators.note: the letter for key goes in the words for a single item

parts.note: a thing is an item or object
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Typing a single entry on a keyboard, one gets annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests typing at a keyboard; it is the musical key C.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin that tingles and wants scratching is irritated, so the word describes that sensation.

clue.text: Blows up virtuous and exemplary individual in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement means each piece retreats, being read backwards in place

parts.note: pure means virtuous or chaste
ST stands for saint, a person of exemplary virtue

explanation.surface: A model citizen loses their temper once they stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns PURE into ERUP and ST into TS, each in its own place.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that explodes violently does this, and so does a person who loses their temper.

clue.text: Spoke of downright newspaper leader

parts.note: utter means downright or complete
ED, short for editor, is the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone talked about a blunt newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspaper leader' suggests an editorial; it is the editor, abbreviated ED. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something aloud is to voice it, which means spoke.

clue.text: An article about bat ting should be found inside

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning
a cricketer batting is said to be in, at the wicket

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on cricket should be found within the pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat ting' is the newspaper's line break of 'batting': in cricket the batting side is in. 'should be found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning in that place or thing, so contained inside.

clue.text: No way!

parts.note: not an exclamation of refusal but a literal description of terrain without any track

explanation.surface: An emphatic refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a flat refusal; taken literally it describes a place with no route through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Untracked terrain with no trail through it lacks any route, literally having no way.

clue.text: Well bound

definitions.meaning: a well is a source of water rising from the ground
a bound is a leap or jump

explanation.definitionFit: A natural water source is a fountainhead, and a leap or jump is a bound.

clue.text: Palestine's potential disadvantages

indicators.note: potential suggests the letters of Palestine could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The Middle Eastern region's possible drawbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' looks like an adjective about the region; it signals that PALESTINE is reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Handicaps imposed in a game or contest put a side at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Present received by a doctor-a sticker

indicators.note: the word for present is received by, so placed inside, the letters for a doctor

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A gift is accepted by a physician who sticks around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift; it means in attendance, as in answering a roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal follower who clings to a cause or surface is one who sticks.

clue.text: A troublesome dog?

parts.note: a hound breed used for hunting hares, which by its name also sounds like one who harasses

explanation.surface: A dog that causes a lot of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: The breed is a hare-hunting hound, but the name also reads as one who harries, that is, pesters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound bred for hunting hares, whose name also suggests a pest who harasses.

clue.text: Green for President!

definitions.meaning: a shade of green cloth named after an English city, worn by Robin Hood's men
Abraham, the sixteenth president of the United States

explanation.definitionFit: A bright woodland colour once worn by archers is named after an English city, and Abraham was the sixteenth US president.

clue.text: Material read, begin revision

indicators.note: revision signals that the letters of read begin are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: Read through again and start making edits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' suggests studying; it signals that READ BEGIN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough woven twill cloth used for raincoats is a fabric, a material.
